title: Affinity-driven KV pool smoothing and compaction orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: design and implement an allocation + background compaction strategy for the KV cache that minimizes long-term fragmentation while preserving continuous-batching latency SLOs. The approach ("Affinity Smoothing") keeps KV allocations aligned with observed batching affinity and temporal locality so that hot sequences occupy contiguous micro-stripes, enabling low-latency access and efficient GPU memory reclamation without disruptive stop-the-world defrags.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end synthetic workload shows >=25% reduction in KV fragmentation metric (measured as free-chunk-count / total-chunks) versus baseline within 24h of steady-state traffic
Tail latency for continuous-batching requests increases by <=5% at P50/P95 during background compaction windows
Background compaction CPU overhead <=8% and GPU memory copy bandwidth stays within configured budget
Feature gated rollout with automatic fallback to previous allocator on regression; canary operates on 10% of serving hosts
Comprehensive telemetry: compaction rate, micro-migration ops, affinity-score distribution, hot-prefix pinning counts, eviction-induced misses
design_notes: Key ideas: (1) Maintain a lightweight affinity score per KV key prefix computed from recent request batching co-occurrence and sequence length distribution. (2) Partition KV pool into small 'micro-stripes' (64–512MB logical units depending on GPU) and aim to pack high-affinity prefixes into contiguous micro-stripes. (3) When allocations cause fragmentation, prefer 'micro-migration' (copy a small set of hot entries to a target contiguous region) during low-util epochs instead of global slab compaction. (4) Implement 'soft anchors' for very hot prefixes so they're exempt from migration unless memory pressure exceeds a higher threshold. (5) Prioritize background compaction tasks by affinity-cluster impact: choose migrations that unlock the largest contiguous runs relevant to active batch affinities. (6) Respect continuous-batching constraints: cap per-request blocking to <200us; use async copy streams and kernel-friendly alignment.
implementation_plan: Phase A - Telemetry & simulation (2w): collect per-prefix batching co-occurrence from production traces; build simulator to evaluate packing heuristics
Phase B - Allocation layer (3w): micro-stripe allocator, affinity scoring API, soft anchors, eviction hint propagation
Phase C - Micro-migration worker (2w): async copy paths, migrator scheduling, graceful pin/unpin, failure rollback
Phase D - Integration & tests (2w): integration with continuous-batching runtime, load tests, GPU bandwidth throttling
Phase E - Canary & rollout (2w): 10% canary -> 30% -> 100% with telemetry gates
telemetry_checks: affinity_score_histogram: ensure stable distribution across time windows
eviction_miss_rate and regen load spikes after migration events
risks: Increased CPU overhead from affinity scoring and migration scheduling—must ensure it doesn't degrade host load for GPU inference
Incorrect affinity heuristics could cause oscillation (migrating data back-and-forth) leading to wasted bandwidth
Edge cases with multi-model buckets: collocating prefixes by affinity might mix conflicting model retention policies
Migration rollbacks under failure could temporarily increase fragmentation and headroom pressure
Complexity of correctness: need strong invariants around pointer validity and KV handles during async moves
testing_plan: Unit: allocator invariants, anchor/unanchor correctness, affinity score boundary tests
Integration: end-to-end with continuous-batching runtime using a staged test harness that can inject pauses and force migrations
Perf: replay 7-day production trace in the simulator to observe steady-state fragmentation and migration churn
Chaos: kill migrator mid-copy, simulate OOM on one GPU, verify automatic rollback and fallback
Canary: small percentage of serving fleet with increased logging, compare against control group dashboards
